debutant.question: Which prophet announced the birth of the Messiah in Bethlehem?
debutant.explanation: Micah 5:2: 'And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah... out of you will come one who will rule over Israel.'

debutant.question: Which prophecy of Isaiah speaks of a virgin giving birth?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 7:14: 'Behold, the virgin will be with child and will bear a son, and they will call his name Immanuel.'

debutant.question: Which prophet announced a 'new heart' for the people?
debutant.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26: 'I will give you a new heart, and put a new spirit within you.'

debutant.question: Who prophesied that dry bones would live again?
debutant.explanation: Ezekiel had a vision of the valley of dry bones coming to life (Ezekiel 37).

debutant.question: What prophecy announces 'a voice crying in the wilderness'?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 40:3 is cited in the 4 gospels to designate John the Baptist preparing the way.

debutant.question: What prophecy foreshadows the king entering Jerusalem on a donkey?
debutant.explanation: Zechariah 9:9 is cited during Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:5).

debutant.question: Which prophet spoke of 'sufferings of the Servant' pierced for our sins?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 53 describes the Suffering Servant 'wounded for our sins, bruised for our iniquities'.

debutant.question: Who prophesied the outpouring of the Spirit upon all flesh?
debutant.explanation: Joel 2:28: 'After this I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.' Peter cites this prophecy at Pentecost (Acts 2:17).

debutant.question: Which prophet announced the new covenant written in the heart?
debutant.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31-34: 'Behold, the days are coming...that I will make a new covenant with Israel.'

debutant.question: Which prophet predicted the return of Elijah before the great day of the Lord?
debutant.explanation: Malachi 4:5: 'Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the day of the LORD comes.'

debutant.question: How many major prophets are in the Old Testament?
debutant.explanation: The 4 major prophets are: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel.

debutant.question: What prophecy speaks of the Messiah being sold for 30 pieces of silver?
debutant.explanation: Zechariah 11:12-13 predicts the 30 pieces of silver—the price of Judas' betrayal (Matthew 27:9).

debutant.question: Who prophesied that the Messiah would be called from Egypt?
debutant.explanation: Hosea 11:1: 'Out of Egypt I have called my son' — fulfilled during Jesus' flight into Egypt (Matthew 2:15).

debutant.question: What prophecy did Daniel interpret for Nebuchadnezzar regarding 4 kingdoms?
options: The vision of the statue of the 4 metals
debutant.explanation: Daniel 2: the statue with a head of gold, chest of silver, belly of bronze and feet of clay represents 4 empires.

debutant.question: What prophet foretold that nations would march to Zion to learn the law?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 2:2-4 / Micah 4:1-3: The nations shall go up to the mountain of the LORD to learn his ways.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that Jesus would be called Emmanuel ('God with us')?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 7:14 says, 'Behold, the girl will conceive and bear a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.'

debutant.question: Which prophet described the Messiah as 'Prince of Peace' and 'Mighty God'?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 9:5-6 names the Messiah as Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the Messiah would be born from the line of David (a branch from the trunk of Jesse)?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 11:1 prophesies that a branch will come out of the trunk of Jesse, the father of King David.

debutant.question: Which book of Psalms begins with the cry 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' spoken by Jesus on the cross?
debutant.explanation: Psalm 22 accurately describes the suffering of crucifixion (pierced hands and feet, garments divided by lot).

debutant.question: According to Psalm 22:18, what did the soldiers do with Messiah's clothing?
options: They threw them into the sea
They returned them to his mother
debutant.explanation: Psalm 22:18 announces: 'They divide my garments among them, they cast lots for my tunic', fulfilled at the foot of the cross (John 19:24).

debutant.question: What Old Testament prophecy predicted that none of the bones of the Messiah would be broken?
debutant.explanation: Psalm 34:20 states 'He keeps all his bones, none of them is broken', quoted at the crucifixion (John 19:36).

debutant.question: Which prophet announced: 'He was wounded for our sins, broken for our iniquities'?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 describes the redeeming suffering of the Servant of the Lord.

debutant.question: Which prophet was swallowed by a large fish for 3 days, foreshadowing the resurrection of Jesus?
debutant.explanation: Jesus himself compares Jonah's 3 days in the fish to his own stay in the tomb (Matthew 12:40).

debutant.question: Which prophet predicted that the Messiah would make the blind see, the deaf hear, and the lame walk?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 35:5-6 announces these messianic healings, which Jesus cites in response to the disciples of John the Baptist (Matthew 11:5).

debutant.question: Which prophet announced the massacre of children in Bethlehem ('Rachel cries for her children')?
debutant.explanation: Matthew 2:17-18 quotes Jeremiah 31:15 during the massacre of the innocents ordered by Herod.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the Messiah would preach 'good news to the poor' (read by Jesus in Nazareth)?
debutant.explanation: At the synagogue in Nazareth, Jesus read Isaiah 61:1-2 and declared: 'Today this word is fulfilled' (Luke 4:18-21).

debutant.question: Who announced the destruction of Jerusalem and an exile to Babylon?
debutant.explanation: Jeremiah warned for forty years that Babylon would destroy Jerusalem if the people did not repent.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the Messiah would be preceded by a messenger preparing the way?
debutant.explanation: Malachi 3:1 announces: 'Behold, I will send my messenger; he will prepare the way before me', fulfilled in John the Baptist.

debutant.question: In which book do we find the prophecy of the statue with feet of clay and iron?
debutant.explanation: Daniel interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the four kingdoms followed by an eternal kingdom established by God (Daniel 2).

debutant.question: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream (Daniel 2), what did the loose stone do without the help of any hand?
options: She breaks the statue and becomes a great mountain filling the whole earth
debutant.explanation: This stone represents the Kingdom of God which will destroy all human kingdoms and endure forever (Daniel 2:34-44).

debutant.question: Which prophet announced the judgment of the world and the coming of a 'Son of man' on the clouds of heaven?
debutant.explanation: Daniel 7:13-14 describes the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven to receive eternal dominion.

debutant.question: Which prophet predicted that swords would be beaten into plowshares and spears into pruning hooks?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4:3 announce this era of universal peace when the nations will no longer learn war.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the righteous king would come to Jerusalem riding on a donkey?
debutant.explanation: Jesus literally fulfilled Zechariah 9:9 during his triumphal entry into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:4-5).

debutant.question: What OT prophecy announces that the Messiah would be despised and rejected by men?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 53:3 describes the Servant as 'despised and forsaken of men, a man of sorrows and accustomed to suffering'.

debutant.question: Which psalm announces: 'You will not abandon my soul to hell, you will not allow your beloved to see corruption'?
debutant.explanation: Peter and Paul cite Psalm 16:10 as a prophecy of Christ's resurrection (Acts 2:27; 13:35).

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the Messiah would be called 'the Lord our righteousness'?
debutant.explanation: Jeremiah 23:5-6 announces a righteous branch raised up in David whose name will be 'The Lord our righteousness'.

debutant.question: Which Genesis prophecy states that the woman's descendants would crush the serpent's head?
debutant.explanation: Genesis 3:15 is called the 'Protegospel', the first promise of victory over Satan through the seed of the woman.

debutant.question: To which patriarch did God promise that all the families of the earth would be blessed in his posterity?
debutant.explanation: God promised Abraham that all nations would be blessed in his descendants, a promise fulfilled in Christ (Galatians 3:8).

debutant.question: From which tribe of Israel was the Messiah (the 'Shiloh') to come according to Jacob's blessing in Genesis 49:10?
debutant.explanation: Jacob prophesied that the scepter would not depart from Judah until Shiloh came (Genesis 49:10).

debutant.question: Which prophet foretold that a star would come out of Jacob and a scepter would arise from Israel?
debutant.explanation: Balaam uttered this messianic oracle on the star of Jacob (Numbers 24:17), recalled by the star of the Magi.

debutant.question: Which prophet did Moses announce that God would raise up among his brothers like him?
debutant.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:15-18 promises a prophet like Moses to whom all Israel must listen—applied to Jesus (Acts 3:22).

debutant.question: Which prophet received a vision of the Lord sitting on a high throne and seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy'?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 6 records his inaugural vision in the Temple and the difficult mission announced to the hardened people.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced the reconstruction of the Temple after the exile by encouraging Zerubbabel and Joshua?
debutant.explanation: Haggai and Zechariah encouraged the people in 520 BC. BC to resume the construction of the Second Temple.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the glory of the second house (the Temple) would be greater than that of the first?
debutant.explanation: Haggai 2:9 promises that the Desired One of all nations will come and fill this house with glory.

debutant.question: Who prophesied in the New Testament the miraculous birth of Jesus to Mary?
debutant.explanation: The angel Gabriel announced to Mary that she would give birth to the Son of the Most High, whose reign will have no end (Luke 1:31-33).

debutant.question: What pious old man in the Temple prophesied that the baby Jesus would be 'a light to enlighten the nations'?
debutant.explanation: Simeon took Jesus in his arms and uttered the song 'Nunc Dimittis', announcing salvation for all people.

debutant.question: What prophecy did Jesus speak about the Temple in Jerusalem to his disciples?
options: That it would last forever without damage
That there would not be one stone left upon another that would not be overturned
That he would be transported to Rome
That it would become a Greek palace
debutant.explanation: Jesus announced the destruction of the Temple (Matthew 24:2), accomplished by the Roman legions in 70 AD. AD

debutant.question: What event did Jesus prophesie to Peter before the rooster crowed?
options: That he would deny him three times
That he would go to Babylon
That he would write a gospel
debutant.explanation: Jesus predicted to Peter that before the rooster crows, he would deny him three times (Matthew 26:34).

debutant.question: What prophecy does the apostle Paul recall in 1 Thessalonians 4 about the return of the Lord?
options: The Lord himself will come down from heaven and the dead in Christ will rise first
debutant.explanation: Paul teaches about the resurrection of the dead in Christ and the catching up of the living to meet the Lord (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17).

debutant.question: Which prophet predicted that the Messiah would be silent before his accusers 'like a lamb led to the slaughter'?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 53:7 describes the silence of the Suffering Servant, a passage the Ethiopian eunuch read in Acts 8:32.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the waters of the Dead Sea would be cleansed by a river flowing from the Temple?
debutant.explanation: Ezekiel 47 describes the river of life flowing out of the sanctuary and healing the Dead Sea until it gave life everywhere.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced the birth of a righteous posterity who will live by their faith ('the righteous will live by their faith')?
debutant.explanation: Habakkuk 2:4 is one of the founding prophetic verses taken up by Paul in Romans 1:17 and Galatians 3:11.

debutant.question: What prophecy from Revelation announces the disappearance of death, mourning and tears?
debutant.explanation: Revelation 21:4 promises that God will wipe away every tear and that death, crying, and pain will be no more.

debutant.question: Which prophet predicted that the Messiah would be betrayed by a close friend who ate his bread?
debutant.explanation: Jesus quotes Psalm 41:9 ('He who ate bread with me has lifted up his heel against me') about Judas (John 13:18).

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that God would offer a free drink to those who thirst (“Come to the waters, all you who are thirsty”)?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 55:1-3 invites freely to the waters and enters into an everlasting covenant according to the graces promised to David.

debutant.question: Which prophet said that God would drive away death forever and wipe away tears from all faces?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 25:8 announces the eschatological feast where God destroys death forever, cited in 1 Corinthians 15:54.

debutant.question: Which prophet in the book of Acts predicted a great famine throughout the earth under Emperor Claudius?
debutant.explanation: Agabus, a prophet who came down from Jerusalem to Antioch, announced by the Spirit a great famine which occurred under Claudius.

debutant.question: Which prophet predicted that Paul would be bound by the Jews in Jerusalem by taking his own girdle?
debutant.explanation: In Caesarea, Agabus took Paul's belt, tied his hands and feet, and announced his arrest in Jerusalem.

debutant.question: What prophecy of Zechariah announces a humble king bringing peace to the nations to the ends of the earth?
debutant.explanation: Zechariah 9:9-10 unites the humility of the king on the colt with his universal reign of peace.

debutant.question: Which prophet announced that the Messiah would bear the sins of many and intercede for the guilty?
debutant.explanation: Isaiah 53:12 is fulfilled on the cross between two evildoers as Jesus prays: 'Father, forgive them' (Luke 23:34).

debutant.question: Which prophet predicted the return of the Jewish people to their land and their future unity under one shepherd ('my servant David')?
debutant.explanation: Ezekiel 34 and 37 announce that God will raise up a single shepherd, his servant David, to feed his united flock.

debutant.question: In the OT parable or prophecy, which prophet broke an earthen pitcher to symbolize the irreversible ruin of Jerusalem?
debutant.explanation: By God's command, Jeremiah broke a potter's pot in the valley of Ben-Hinnom before the elders (Jeremiah 19:10-11).

intermediaire.question: How long was the Babylonian exile prophesied by Jeremiah?
intermediaire.explanation: Jeremiah 25:11-12 and 29:10: the exile would last 70 years before the return.

intermediaire.question: What does the 'cornerstone' represent in Isaiah 28:16?
options: A precious foundation laid by God symbolizing the Messiah
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 28:16: 'I lay in Zion a stone, a proven stone, a cornerstone, precious' — cited by Peter (1 Peter 2:6) for Christ.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy of Micah also announces the context of the messianic birth?
intermediaire.explanation: Micah 5:2: 'And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah... out of you will come for me one who is to rule over Israel, whose origin is from ancient times.'

intermediaire.question: What does the '70 weeks' prophecy describe in Daniel 9?
options: The period leading to the coming of the Messiah and the end of the Temple
intermediaire.explanation: Daniel 9:24-27: The 70 weeks of years cover the period up to the Messiah-Prince and the destruction of the Temple.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy of Isaiah describes the reign of messianic peace with the wolf and the lamb?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 11:6-9: 'The wolf will dwell with the lamb...for the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD.'

intermediaire.question: In Isaiah 9:6, what is one of the messianic names that means 'Everlasting Father'?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 9:6 lists 4 names: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace.

intermediaire.question: What prophecy of Zechariah says that they will look upon him whom they have pierced?
intermediaire.explanation: Zechariah 12:10: 'They will look upon me whom they have pierced' — cited in John 19:37.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet used his own married life as a living prophecy?
intermediaire.explanation: Hosea married Gomer, an unfaithful woman, to symbolize Israel's unfaithfulness and God's faithful love.

intermediaire.question: What did Ezekiel 37 prophesy with the vision of the bones?
options: The creation of a new alliance
intermediaire.explanation: Ezekiel 37 is a metaphor for the national and spiritual restoration of scattered Israel.

intermediaire.question: In which prophecy is the Messiah called 'Branch of David'?
intermediaire.explanation: The Davidic 'Branch' or 'Branch' appears in Isaiah (11:1), Jeremiah (23:5; 33:15), Zechariah (3:8; 6:12).

intermediaire.question: What does the prophecy of 'the day of the Lord' in Amos 5:18 mean?
options: A warning: it will be a day of darkness, no light for those who seek the judgment of others
intermediaire.explanation: Amos turns the popular expectation upside down: the 'Day of the Lord' will be darkness for a disobedient Israel.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy speaks of the Messiah as 'Light to the nations'?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 49:6: 'I will make you a light to the nations, to carry my salvation to the ends of the earth.'

intermediaire.question: Which prophet prophesied the judgment of Nineveh, the Assyrian capital?
intermediaire.explanation: The book of Nahum is entirely devoted to the prophecy of the judgment of Nineveh, fulfilled in 612 BC. AD

intermediaire.question: What does Joel 2:28-32 prophesy fulfilled according to Peter at Pentecost?
options: The coming of John the Baptist
The outpouring of the Spirit on all flesh with prophetic signs
intermediaire.explanation: Peter cites Joel 2:28-32 in Acts 2:17-21 to explain Pentecost.

intermediaire.question: What is the prophecy of the 'suffering maid' of Isaiah 52:13-53:12?
options: The portrait of the Messiah suffering, rejected, bearing our sins
A description of the Babylonian exile
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 52:13-53:12 is the 4th Servant song, cited more than 40 times in the NT for Christ.

intermediaire.question: Which royal psalm prophesies: 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand'?
intermediaire.explanation: Psalm 110:1 is the OT text most frequently cited in the NT to designate the exaltation of Christ (Matthew 22:44; Acts 2:34).

intermediaire.question: Which psalm prophesies that the Messiah is 'a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek'?
intermediaire.explanation: Psalm 110:4 combines messianic kingship and the eternal priesthood of Melchizedek, developed in Hebrews 5-7.

intermediaire.question: Which messianic psalm declares: 'You are my Son, this day have I begotten you'?
intermediaire.explanation: Psalm 2:7 is cited at Jesus' baptism, resurrection (Acts 13:33) and in Hebrews 1:5.

intermediaire.question: Which psalm announces: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief of the corner'?
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus and Peter apply Psalm 118:22 to the religious leaders' rejection of the Messiah and his victory (Matthew 21:42; Acts 4:11).

intermediaire.question: Which prophet used a wooden yoke on his neck to symbolize submission to Babylon?
intermediaire.explanation: Jeremiah bore a yoke to exhort the nations to submit to Nebuchadnezzar; Hananiah broke it and was replaced by a yoke of iron.

intermediaire.question: What prophetic sign does Ezekiel fulfill by lying on his left side then on his right side?
options: The years of iniquity of Israel (390 days) and Judah (40 days)
intermediaire.explanation: In Ezekiel 4:4-6, the prophet symbolically bears the iniquity of Israel and Judah for one day for one year.

intermediaire.question: What did Micah 3:12 predict about Zion and Jerusalem, a prophecy later recalled to save Jeremiah?
options: That Zion would be plowed like a field and Jerusalem would become a heap of stones
That the Temple would become gold
intermediaire.explanation: In Jeremiah 26:18, the elders cite Micah of Moresheth to remind us that a prophet had already announced the ruin of Jerusalem.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy from Zechariah (11:12-13) associates the 30 silver coins with the 'potter's field'?
options: Zechariah asks for his wages and throws it into the house of the Lord for the potter
intermediaire.explanation: Matthew 27:9-10 connects Judas' betrayal for 30 pieces of silver and purchase of the potter's field to Zechariah 11 and Jeremiah.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet said: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered'?
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus quotes Zechariah 13:7 on the night of Gethsemane to announce the dispersion of his disciples (Matthew 26:31).

intermediaire.question: What prophet announced that the pagan nations would know the name of God, from the east to the west?
intermediaire.explanation: Malachi 1:11 declares that from the rising of the sun to the setting of the sun, the name of the LORD is great among the nations.

intermediaire.question: In Daniel 7, what do the four great animals coming out of the sea represent?
options: Four successive kingdoms/empires that will arise on the earth
intermediaire.explanation: The four beasts (lion, bear, leopard, fearsome beast) correspond to four successive empires (Daniel 7:17).

intermediaire.question: In Daniel 8, what do the ram with two horns and the hairy goat with a large horn between the eyes represent?
options: The Medo-Persian Empire (ram) defeated by the Greek Empire of Alexander the Great (goat)
intermediaire.explanation: Daniel 8:20-21 explicitly identifies the ram with the kings of the Medes and the Persians, and the goat with the king of Javan (Greece).

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced the judgment of Edom for its betrayal of its brother Jacob during the fall of Jerusalem?
intermediaire.explanation: The entire book of Obadiah is a prophecy against Edom's pride and violence toward Judah (Obadiah 10-15).

intermediaire.question: What prophecy from Amos (9:11) is cited by James at the Council of Jerusalem to justify welcoming non-Jews?
options: 'I will raise up the tent of David from its fall' so that the rest of men will seek the Lord
intermediaire.explanation: Acts 15:16-17 cites Amos 9:11-12 to show that the inclusion of the nations was foretold by the prophets.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet predicted by name the Persian king Cyrus more than a century before his birth as God's instrument to rebuild Jerusalem?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 44:28-45:1 names Cyrus as 'my shepherd' and 'his anointed' to deliver the exiles and rebuild the Temple.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet received a vision of a golden lampstand powered by two olive trees with the words: 'Neither by power, nor by might, but by my Spirit'?
intermediaire.explanation: Zechariah 4:6 encourages Zerubbabel to complete the Temple not by human power but by the Spirit of the Lord.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy from Isaiah (42:1-4) describes the Servant who 'will not break a broken reed or quench a smoking wick'?
options: The first song of the Servant
intermediaire.explanation: Matthew 12:18-21 cites Isaiah 42:1-4 to describe the gentleness and righteousness of Jesus' ministry.

intermediaire.question: In Matthew 2:23, 'He will be called a Nazarene' likely refers to what Hebrew prophetic pun?
intermediaire.explanation: Several commentators see a link with 'netzer' (offspring/branch) in Isaiah 11:1 as well as with the contempt attached to Nazareth.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced that light would first shine on 'the Galilee of the nations' (lands of Zebulun and Naphtali)?
intermediaire.explanation: Matthew 4:14-16 quotes Isaiah 9:1-2 when Jesus begins his public ministry in Galilee at Capernaum.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet predicted that a voice of lamentation would be heard over Jerusalem, but also a new covenant with forgiveness of sins?
intermediaire.explanation: Jeremiah 31 announces both Rachel's tears and the New Covenant engraved in hearts (31:31-34).

intermediaire.question: Which prophet was ordered to purchase a field in Anathoth while the Babylonian army was besieging Jerusalem?
intermediaire.explanation: By purchasing his cousin Hanameel's field in the midst of a siege, Jeremiah prophesied by deed that life and land would return to Judah (Jeremiah 32:15).

intermediaire.question: What OT prophecy predicts a king who will 'judge between many peoples' and whose peace will have no end?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 9:6-7 promises endless increase to the dominion and peace of David's throne.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet predicted the three and a half year drought under Ahab before praying for the return of rain?
intermediaire.explanation: Elijah announced that there would be neither dew nor rain except for his word (1 Kings 17:1; James 5:17).

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced to Jeroboam I the tearing of the kingdom by tearing a new coat into 12 pieces?
intermediaire.explanation: Ahijah gave 10 pieces to Jeroboam, announcing that Solomon would lose 10 tribes to idolatry.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced that a king named Josiah would burn human bones on the idolatrous altar at Bethel?
options: A man of God from Judah (1 Kings 13:2)
intermediaire.explanation: Three centuries before Josiah, this man of God named Josiah before the altar of Bethel; the prophecy is fulfilled in 2 Kings 23:15-16.

intermediaire.question: In Revelation, what do the 'two witnesses' who prophesy of 1260 days clothed in sackcloth represent (Revelation 11)?
options: The prophetic witness of the Church (recalling Moses and Elijah) to the nations
intermediaire.explanation: Clothed with the powers of Moses (water changed into blood) and Elijah (closing the sky), they represent the faithful prophetic testimony to the end.

intermediaire.question: What do the 'seven seals', 'seven trumpets' and 'seven vials' symbolize in the book of Revelation?
options: Cycles of divine judgments and warnings leading to final judgment and the Kingdom of God
The 7 wonders of the ancient world
intermediaire.explanation: These three septenaries structure the apocalyptic revelation of the progressive judgment on a rebellious world and the victory of the Lamb.

intermediaire.question: What prophecy of Paul's in Romans 11 foreshadows Israel's spiritual future?
options: Let a partial hardening come upon Israel until all the Gentiles have entered, and thus all Israel will be saved
That Rome will replace the Bible
That the Law of Moses is canceled for the Jews
intermediaire.explanation: Romans 11:25-26 reveals this 'mystery' of God's irrevocable faithfulness to the promises made to the fathers.

intermediaire.question: In 2 Thessalonians 2, what must happen before the Day of the Lord?
options: The apostasy and the revelation of the 'ungodly man' (son of perdition)
The construction of a tower at Babel
intermediaire.explanation: Paul warns against thinking that the day of the Lord is already here, recalling the apostasy and the ungodly sitting in the temple of God.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy of Jesus in Luke 21:24 connects the fall of Jerusalem to a specific historical period?
options: 'Jerusalem will be trodden down by the nations, until the times of the nations are fulfilled'
'The Jordan will disappear in one day'
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus announces the ruin of Jerusalem in 70 AD. BC and a temporal limit set by God ('the times of the nations').

intermediaire.question: Which prophet described the collapse of proud Tyre, a Phoenician maritime city?
intermediaire.explanation: Ezekiel prophesied that Tire would be razed and its rubble thrown into the sea, which was notably accomplished during the siege of Alexander the Great.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced that the people sitting in darkness would see a great light?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 9:1-2 prophesies of a great light rising upon those who dwell in the land of the shadow of death.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy from Psalm 69:9 ('The zeal of your house devours me') is applied to Jesus by the disciples?
options: When he drives out the merchants from the Temple (John 2:17)
intermediaire.explanation: As his disciples saw Jesus purifying the Temple in Jerusalem, they remembered this word from Psalm 69:9.

intermediaire.question: Which verse from Psalm 69:21 foreshadowed the vinegar presented to Jesus on the cross?
options: 'They put gall in my food, and to quench my thirst they drink vinegar over me'
intermediaire.explanation: John 19:28-29 highlights the fulfillment of Scripture when Jesus said 'I thirst' and was given vinegar.

intermediaire.question: What prophet announced that a river of grace would heal the bitterness and barrenness of the earth (Ezekiel 47)—what tree grows on its banks?
options: Trees bearing fruit every month and whose leaves are used for healing
intermediaire.explanation: This vision from Ezekiel 47:12 is repeated almost word for word for the tree of life in the New Jerusalem (Revelation 22:2).

intermediaire.question: In the prophecy of Daniel 12:2, what does it clearly say about the dead?
options: Let them sleep forever without waking up
'Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life...'
intermediaire.explanation: Daniel 12:2 is one of the most explicit affirmations of individual resurrection and final judgment in the Old Testament.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet saw the Lord holding a plumb line (level) to measure the righteousness of Israel?
intermediaire.explanation: The vision of the plumb line in Amos 7 shows that the time for forgiveness without repentance has passed for the northern kingdom.

intermediaire.question: What prophet predicted that a famine would come, not from bread and water, but from hearing the words of the Lord?
intermediaire.explanation: Amos 8:11 warns that persistent rejection of the prophetic word will lead to a painful silence from God.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy in Zechariah 3 shows the high priest Joshua clothed in filthy garments and then cleansed by the Angel of the Lord?
options: A vision announcing the forgiveness of Israel's sins and the coming of the 'Branch' in a single day
intermediaire.explanation: Zechariah 3:8-9 announces that God will remove the iniquity of the land in one day through his servant the Branch.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced that the tail of a Jew's garment would be seized, saying: 'We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you'?
intermediaire.explanation: Zechariah 8:23 announces the spiritual attraction of the nations to Jerusalem and the God of Israel.

intermediaire.question: Which prophecy in Isaiah 19 surprisingly announces the future reconciliation of three ancient enemies: Egypt, Assyria and Israel?
options: 'Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance'
'Egypt and Assyria will be erased forever'
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 19:24-25 offers a striking universal vision where former oppressors become God's people with Israel.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet described horses of four colors (red, black, white, spotted) patrolling the earth?
intermediaire.explanation: The visions of the horsemen and the four chariots in Zechariah directly inspired the four horsemen of the Apocalypse (Revelation 6).

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced: 'For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the depths of the sea by the waters that cover it'?
intermediaire.explanation: Habakkuk 2:14 (close to Isaiah 11:9) affirms that God's glory will ultimately fill all creation.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet told Hezekiah that the treasures of his palace would one day be taken to Babylon?
intermediaire.explanation: After Hezekiah showed his riches to Babylon's envoys, Isaiah prophesied the future Babylonian deportation.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet predicted that the Messiah would make his soul a guilt offering (asham) and see a posterity prolong his days?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 53:10 announces both the Servant's atoning death and his victory/resurrection ('he will prolong his days').

intermediaire.question: Which prophet announced that the God of Israel would bring 'fishermen' and 'hunters' to bring back his scattered people?
intermediaire.explanation: Jeremiah 16:14-16 announces a new exodus greater than that of Egypt.

intermediaire.question: In the Acts of the Apostles, which OT prophet does Peter cite to explain the death and replacement of Judas?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter quotes these two psalms in Acts 1:20 before casting lots for Matthias to replace Judas.

expert.question: What is the structure of the 4 'Servant songs' in Isaiah?
expert.explanation: The 4 songs of the Servant are: Isaiah 42:1-9; 49:1-13; 50:4-11; 52:13-53:12.

expert.question: What does the Hebrew term 'almah' mean in Isaiah 7:14 and why is it debated?
options: It only means 'young woman' with no implication of virginity
'Almah' designates a young woman of marriageable age, often a virgin; the Septuagint translates as 'parthenos' (virgin)
It's a technical term for prophecy
expert.explanation: 'Almah' (עַלְמָה) = young woman of marriageable age. The LXX translates it 'parthenos' (virgin). Matthew 1:23 cites the LXX for fulfillment in Mary.

expert.question: What is the hermeneutical debate on the prophecy of double fulfillment (sensus plenior)?
options: Prophecies only have a literal meaning
The 'sensus plenior' recognizes an immediate literal meaning AND a deeper fulfillment intended by God in Christ
The prophecies have only an allegorical meaning
There are no messianic prophecies in the OT
expert.explanation: The 'sensus plenior' (fuller meaning): the human author prophesies for his immediate context, but God inscribes a deeper fulfillment (eg Hosea 11:1 cited in Mt 2:15).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the '70 weeks' in Daniel 9:24 according to different interpretations?
options: 70 weeks of years = 490 years, covering different periods depending on interpretations (historical, eschatological)
A symbolic number without precise chronology
Only a prophecy already fulfilled in 70 AD. AD
expert.explanation: Daniel 9: 70 weeks = 70 × 7 years = 490 years. Debate between: (1) total accomplishment in 70 AD. AD; (2) future eschatological final week; (3) purely symbolic interpretation.

expert.question: What is the theological significance of 'Servant of the Lord' in Isaiah 40-55 (Deutero-Isaiah)?
options: The Servant is exclusively collective Israel
The Servant oscillates between collective Israel and an individual figure, culminating in the portrait of a substitute innocent in Isaiah 53
The Servant is only a historical figure (Cyrus)
The Servant is exclusively the prophet Isaiah himself
expert.explanation: The tension is intentional: the Servant is sometimes Israel (42:19; 49:3), sometimes distinct from Israel (49:5-6; 53), converging on a suffering individual figure.

expert.question: How does the typological method differ from allegorism in prophetic interpretation?
options: The typology preserves the literal historical meaning as a real type prefiguring its antitype; allegorism replaces literal meaning with arbitrary spiritual meaning
The typology is post-apostolic, the allegorism is apostolic
Allegorism is more rigorous than typology
expert.explanation: Crucial distinction: (1) Typological—the actual historical events of the OT prefigure their Christological fulfillment; (2) Allegorical — the literal meaning becomes pure symbol without historical basis.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew term 'nabi' (prophet) in its fundamental dimension?
options: 'Nabi' designates one who speaks in the name of God - spokesperson (forth-telling) as well as predictor (foretelling)
expert.explanation: 'Nabi' (נָבִיא): the prophet is first and foremost a spokesperson for God for his present time (forth-telling). Prediction (foretelling) is one dimension among others.

expert.question: What is the relationship between the prophecy of Jeremiah 31:31-34 and the book of Hebrews?
options: Hebrews 8:8-12 quotes Jeremiah 31 in full to demonstrate that the New Covenant in Christ makes the Old Obsolete
Hebrews cites Jeremiah to defend the Mosaic Law
Jeremiah 31 is interpreted allegorically only in Hebrews
expert.explanation: Hebrews 8:8-12 is the longest OT quotation in the NT — Jeremiah 31:31-34 demonstrating the superiority of the New Covenant.

expert.question: To what extent is the prophecy of Isaiah 40:3 (the voice in the wilderness) 'fulfilled' in the NT?
options: It is not mentioned in the NT
The 4 gospels cite it for John the Baptist, but with different modifications revealing their own Christology
It is only mentioned in John
expert.explanation: Matthew (3:3), Mark (1:3), Luke (3:4-6), John (1:23) all quote Isaiah 40:3. But Luke also cites Isaiah 40:4-5 to emphasize the universal scope.

expert.question: What is the eschatological meaning of the 'resurrection' in Ezekiel 37 versus Isaiah 26:19?
options: Both texts speak only of individual resurrection
Ezekiel 37 is national metaphor; Isaiah 26:19 tends more toward actual individual resurrection
Both are allegories without eschatological meaning
expert.explanation: Ezekiel 37 = national restoration of Israel (metaphor). Isaiah 26:19: 'Your dead will live, my corpses will rise' tends towards a hope of individual resurrection.

expert.question: What is the messianic prophecy implicit in Psalm 22 and its relationship to the Passion?
options: Psalm 22 contains multiple details (mockery, sharing of clothes, thirst) cited in the Passion stories
This is purely a complaint from historical David
Only verse 1 ("My God, my God...") is relevant
expert.explanation: Psalm 22 is massively cited in the Passion stories: v.1 (Mt 27:46), v.7-8 (Mt 27:39-43), v.16 (Jn 19:37), v.18 (Jn 19:24).

expert.question: How to interpret the prophecy of 'Gog and Magog' from Ezekiel 38-39?
options: Eschatological symbol of a final enemy coalition against Israel, taken up in Revelation 20
expert.explanation: Gog/Magog (Ez 38-39): symbolic eschatological context taken up in Revelation 20:8. Interpretations vary: literal future (dispensationalism), symbolic (amillennialism).

expert.question: What prophecy of Zephaniah foreshadows the humble 'faithful remnant' who will inherit the promises?
expert.explanation: Zephaniah 3:12-13: 'I will leave among you a people humble and poor; they will trust in the name of the Lord.' — foundation of the concept of the 'remainder' in the Beatitudes.

expert.question: What is the relationship between the prophecy of the 'Son of man in the clouds' (Daniel 7:13) and Mark's Christology?
options: Jesus explicitly applies Daniel 7:13 during his trial (Mark 14:62), claiming identity as the divine Son of Man
expert.explanation: Mark 14:62: Jesus said to the high priest 'you will see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of power and coming on the clouds' — direct quote from Daniel 7:13 + Psalm 110:1.

expert.question: What is the prophecy of Isaiah 11:1-10 and its triple messianic dimension?
options: A offspring of Jesse: (1) endowed with the Spirit of 7 gifts, (2) ruling with justice for the poor, (3) restoring creation (cosmic peace)
expert.explanation: Isaiah 11: (1) the anointing of the Spirit (v.1-3); (2) righteous rule for the humble (v.4-5); (3) cosmic peace restored (v.6-9) — three complementary messianic dimensions.

expert.question: Why is Isaiah 53:4 cited differently in Matthew 8:17 versus 1 Peter 2:24?
options: Matthew applies the verse to Jesus' physical healings; Peter applies it to sin — illustrating the hermeneutical richness of the text
expert.explanation: Isaiah 53:4: Matthew 8:17 = healings (literal meaning of illnesses); 1 Peter 2:24 = sins. Both are legitimate because the Hebrew text contains both dimensions.

expert.question: What do we call the literary genre of prophecies structured as a legal trial in which God sues Israel for breaking the covenant?
expert.explanation: The prophetic 'rîb' takes up the structure of treaties of suzerainty: summoning of witnesses (heavens and earth), reminder of benefits, accusation and sentence.

expert.question: What is the function of 'prophetic telescopy' (peak perspective) in the interpretation of biblical prophecies?
options: Predict exact dates to the day
See the first and second coming of Christ aligned on the same horizon like two distant peaks without distinguishing the valley between the two
Read only the literal geographic meaning
expert.explanation: As in Isaiah 61:1-2 (where Jesus pauses before 'the day of vengeance'), the prophets contemplate initial salvation and final consummation together.

expert.question: Which oracle in Isaiah 7:14-16 first had a short-term sign for King Ahaz before its full fulfillment in Jesus?
options: Before the child knows how to reject evil and choose good, the two enemy kings (Damascus and Samaria) will be abandoned
Babylon will destroy Rome in 3 years
Elijah will return in his lifetime
expert.explanation: The oracle responded to the crisis of 735 BC. (rapid sign in a few years) while carrying a plenary messianic promise fulfilled in Matthew 1:23.

expert.question: In Hosea 11:1 ('I have called my son out of Egypt'), how does Matthew 2:15 use this text?
options: By typological reading: Jesus perfectly recapitulates and completes the history of Israel as the faithful Son of God
To prove that Moses had returned
expert.explanation: In Hosea 11:1, 'my son' refers to Israel in the Exodus; Matthew sees an accomplished type in Jesus, true Israel.

expert.question: What is the difference between classical (pre-exilic) prophecy and apocalyptic (exilic/post-exilic like Daniel and Zechariah 9-14)?
options: Classical prophecy calls for repentance in present history; the apocalyptic reveals through symbolic visions the sovereign cosmic outcome in the face of evil
The apocalyptic never talks about God
expert.explanation: The apocalyptic arises in times of extreme crisis (exile, persecution) with interpreting angels, cosmic dualism and the final triumph of God.

expert.question: In Jeremiah 29:10-14, what chronological standard does God give to the promise of restoration?
options: Only when 70 years are completed for Babylon
expert.explanation: Against the optimistic false prophets (Jeremiah 28), Jeremiah announces a 70-year exile and exhorts the exiles to build and pray for Babylon.

expert.question: In Daniel 9:2, what Bible text was Daniel studying when he realized the end of the exile was near?
options: The scrolls of the prophet Jeremiah announcing 70 years of desolation
expert.explanation: Daniel 9:2 explicitly mentions his reading of the books and the number of years revealed by the Lord to the prophet Jeremiah.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the '70 weeks' (490 years) divided into 7 + 62 + 1 weeks in Daniel 9:24-27?
options: They culminate in the atonement of iniquity, the coming of a cut-off Anointed One (Messiah), then the destruction of the city and the sanctuary
They only concern creation in 6 days
They predict the length of Saul's reign
expert.explanation: Daniel 9:24-27 announces six saving blessings and the strengthened covenant after the cutting off of an Anointed One and the ruin of the sanctuary.

expert.question: What is the role of the 'Go'el' (redeemer) in Job 19:25 ('I know that my redeemer lives')?
options: A simple human lawyer in Jerusalem
A divine defender and guarantor who will take up the cause of the righteous even beyond death
expert.explanation: Job's hope beyond injustice presents a living Avenger/Redeemer who will rise from the dust and allow him to see God.

expert.question: Why is Jeremiah 18:7-10 crucial for understanding the 'conditionality' of certain prophecies of judgment or blessing?
options: Because God declares that if a nation prophesied to do evil repents, He renounces the evil He intended to do to them (like Nineveh in Jonah)
Because the prophets invent their messages
Because God never changes his method
expert.explanation: Jeremiah 18 states the principle of moral response: the oracles of judgment call for repentance to avoid sentence (Jonah 3:10).

expert.question: In Deuteronomy 13:1-5 and 18:20-22, what two complementary tests allow us to discern a true prophet from a false prophet?
options: The fulfillment of his predictions AND his doctrinal fidelity to the one true God (YHWH)
expert.explanation: Even if a sign is fulfilled, if it leads to other gods (Dt 13), it is a false prophet; likewise, a word that is not fulfilled does not come from God (Dt 18).

expert.question: In Acts 2:17-21, why does Peter change 'after this' (Joel 2:28) to 'in the last days'?
options: To emphasize theologically that the outpouring of the Spirit at Pentecost inaugurates the final eschatological era ('the last days')
expert.explanation: From the NT perspective, the 'last days' begin with the first coming of Christ and the outpouring of the Spirit until the Parousia.

expert.question: What is the classic interpretation of the 'restrictor' (to katechon / ho katechôn) mentioned by Paul in 2 Thessalonians 2:6-7?
options: Traditionally identified with Roman imperial order/civil authority, or the action of the Holy Spirit restraining the unleashing of evil until the appointed time
expert.explanation: The Fathers (Tertullian, Chrysostom) often saw the Roman Empire maintaining order; others see it as the Holy Spirit or God's sovereign design.

expert.question: In Romans 11:26, what are the three main interpretations of the phrase 'all Israel will be saved'?
options: (1) All Jewish and pagan elected officials; (2) the faithful remnant of Israel throughout the ages; (3) a mass conversion of the Jewish people at the end of time
expert.explanation: Exegetes debate between spiritual Israel (Calvin), the sum of the Jewish elect remnant, or a final awakening of ethnic Israel before the Parousia.

expert.question: What is the significance of the oracle of Zechariah 12:10 ('They will look to me whom they have pierced') in NT Christology?
options: Quoted in John 19:37 (pierced side of Jesus) and Revelation 1:7 (glorious return) — where YHWH himself says 'unto me' they pierced
expert.explanation: In the Hebrew text, YHWH speaks in the first person ('to me, whom they pierced'), emphasizing the divine identity of the crucified Christ.

expert.question: In Ezekiel 40-48, what are the two main readings of the vision of the eschatological Temple?
options: Either a literal vision of a future millennial temple or a symbolic vision of God's perfect presence with his people (fulfilled in Christ and the New Jerusalem)
A simple description of the Tabernacle of Moses
expert.explanation: The dispensationalist interpretation expects a literal future temple, while the Christocentric/amillennialist approach sees it as a symbol of perfect worship in Christ (Rev 21:22).

expert.question: Which prophetic text from Isaiah 52:7 ('How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news') is cited by Paul in Romans 10:15?
options: To justify the need for missionary preaching of the Gospel
To talk about the architecture of the Temple
expert.explanation: Paul applies the announcement of the deliverance of Zion to the messengers of the Gospel of peace sent to all nations.

expert.question: How does Hebrews 8:8-13 use the prophecy of Jeremiah 31:31-34 about the New Covenant?
options: To show that the old covenant was perfect and final
To prove that from the OT God announced a superior alliance making the old Levitical alliance obsolete
To reject the entire Old Testament
expert.explanation: The author of Hebrews notes that the word 'new' in Jeremiah's pen thereby renders the old covenant obsolete and ready to disappear.

expert.question: In Revelation, which prophecy from Isaiah 65:17 and 66:22 establishes the final hope of the book?
options: The creation of new heavens and a new earth
Return to the Golden Age of Babylon
expert.explanation: Revelation 21:1 takes directly from Isaiah 65:17 to describe the final cosmic renewal where God dwells with men.

expert.question: In Micah 5:1-3 (5:2-4), what paradoxical origin is attributed to the future ruler born in Bethlehem?
options: He came from Egypt 10 years ago
'Its origins go back to ancient times, to the days of eternity'
He has no connection with David
expert.explanation: Alongside the smallness of Bethlehem Ephrata, Micah affirms the mysterious (even eternal) seniority of the Messiah.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the symbolic name 'Lo-Ammi' ('Not my people') given to the son of the prophet Hosea (Hosea 1:9)?
options: The temporary breaking of the covenant following Israel's unfaithfulness, followed by a promise of restoration ('Ammi', my people)
expert.explanation: Peter (1 Peter 2:10) and Paul (Romans 9:25) apply this reversal of Hosea 2:23 to Gentile believers who have become God's people.

expert.question: What is the role of 'songs of the vineyard' in Isaiah 5:1-7 and how does Jesus take it up in Matthew 21:33-43?
options: Isaiah compares Israel to an ungrateful vine; Jesus takes up the image with murderous winegrowers who kill the Son to announce the transfer of the Kingdom
They celebrate the wine of Cana
expert.explanation: Jesus' listeners immediately understood that the parable of the vineyard workers was aimed at their rejection of the prophets and the Son (Matthew 21:45).

expert.question: In Zechariah 6:12-13, what messianic title uniquely unites the royal and priestly functions?
options: The 'Sprout' (Tsemah) who will build the Temple of the Lord and be priest on his throne
expert.explanation: Under the Mosaic Law, king (Judah) and priest (Levi) were separated; Zechariah 6:13 announces their harmonious union in the Germ.

expert.question: Which prophet of the 8th century BC? AD announced the fall of Samaria while promising a remnant gathered like sheep to the fold (Micah 2:12)?
expert.explanation: Micah alternates oracles of uncompromising judgment on Samaria and Jerusalem with luminous promises of messianic gathering.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the oracle in Zephaniah 3:9 promising 'clean lips' to the people?
options: The conversion of the nations who will all call on the name of the Lord and serve him with one accord
expert.explanation: Zephaniah 3:9 announces the universalization of pure worship after the judgment, in contrast to the confusion of the tongues of Babel.

expert.question: Which prophecy in Daniel 11:31 announces 'the abomination that causes desolation', an expression taken up by Jesus in Matthew 24:15?
options: The desecration of the Temple by Antiochus IV (167 BC), which became the type of eschatological desecration and the siege of 70 AD. AD
La construction du Temple de Salomon
The passage of the Red Sea
expert.explanation: The historical fulfillment under Antiochus IV Epiphanes serves as Jesus' prophetic model for the Jerusalem crisis and the end times.

expert.question: In Isaiah 49:6, why does God declare that the restoration of just the tribes of Israel is 'a small thing' to the Servant?
options: Because He established him to be the 'light of the nations', so that his salvation would reach to the ends of the earth
Because the earth will disappear immediately
expert.explanation: Paul and Barnabas cite Isaiah 49:6 in Antioch of Pisidia (Acts 13:47) to justify their mission to the Gentiles.

expert.question: What is the paradox of Psalm 110:1 raised by Jesus before the Pharisees in Matthew 22:41-45?
options: How can the Messiah be both David's son (descendant) and his 'Lord'?
Why did David write this psalm in Greek?
How many soldiers did David have?
expert.explanation: Jesus shows that the Messiah is more than just a human king descended from David: he is the divine Lord seated at the right hand of God.

expert.question: In 1 Peter 1:10-12, what does the apostle reveal about the OT prophets' awareness of their own oracles?
options: They searched out the times and circumstances that marked the Spirit of Christ in them, finding that they were serving our generation.
They were not inspired by the Spirit
expert.explanation: 1 Peter 1:10-12 illuminates the double dimension of prophecy: the prophets scrutinized the mystery of Christ's sufferings and subsequent glories.

expert.question: Which OT prophecy is cited in Romans 15:9-12 to prove the common worship of Jews and Gentiles?
options: A sequence of four texts (2 Sam 22 / Ps 18, Dt 32:43, Ps 117:1, Isaiah 11:10)
expert.explanation: Paul weaves together quotes from the Law, Psalms, and Prophets (all three parts of the Hebrew Bible) to demonstrate the inclusion of the nations.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the image of the 'stone that came out of the mountain' (Daniel 2) in relation to the 'corner stone' (Isaiah 28:16 / Ps 118:22)?
options: The same Christology of the Stone: foundation and corner stone for those who believe, stone of fall and judgment that shatters rebellious kingdoms
Two stones from the Sinai desert
expert.explanation: Luke 20:17-18 and 1 Peter 2:6-8 synthesize these texts: the rejected stone becomes a corner stone or a crushing stone.

expert.question: In Malachi 4:5-6 (3:23-24), how does Jesus interpret the promise of the prophet Elijah coming before the Day of the Lord?
options: He says Elijah will never come
He identifies John the Baptist as the 'Elijah who was to come' in the spirit and power of Elijah (Matthew 11:14; 17:12)
expert.explanation: The angel Gabriel (Luke 1:17) and Jesus (Matthew 11:14) apply Malachi's oracle to the preparatory ministry of John the Baptist.

expert.question: Which prophecy from Jeremiah 7:11 does Jesus cite in cleansing the Temple ('You have made it a den of thieves')?
options: A warning against false religious security which believes the Temple inviolable despite moral injustice
A rule on the price of doves
expert.explanation: In Jeremiah 7, the prophet denounced the illusion 'This is the Temple of the Lord!' ; Jesus updates exactly this prophetic criticism.

expert.question: In Revelation, what does the phrase 'the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy' (Revelation 19:10) mean?
options: All true biblical prophecy has as its center, goal and source the testimony to Jesus Christ
Prophecy ceased in the Old Testament
expert.explanation: The angel refuses John's adoration and reminds us that all prophetic inspiration converges on the person and work of Christ.

expert.question: What is the difference between the majority Jewish messianic expectation of the 1st century and the prophetic portrait of Jesus in the Gospels?
options: The majority expectation hoped for an immediate triumphant political/military Messiah, struggling to integrate the Suffering Servant of Isaiah 53 before glory
They were waiting for a Messiah from Rome
expert.explanation: This is why Jesus explained on the road to Emmaus (Luke 24:26) that Christ had to suffer these things before entering into his glory.

expert.question: In Isaiah 6:9-10 ('Listen carefully, but do not understand'), why does Jesus cite this prophecy to explain the parables (Mark 4:12)?
options: Because parables reveal the mysteries of the Kingdom to humble hearts while manifesting judgment on those who harden themselves
expert.explanation: The parables accomplish the double effect of the prophetic word of Isaiah 6: to enlighten the disciples and leave the unbelievers in their voluntary hardness.

expert.question: Which prophet described the final spiritual restoration of Israel as spring and autumn rain (Hosea 6:3) and healing from unfaithfulness (Hosea 14)?
expert.explanation: Hosea concludes his book of judgment with a magnificent promise of free healing and spiritual fruitfulness (Hosea 14:4-8).

expert.question: In Ezekiel 28:11-19, the lament over the king of Tire uses Edenic images ('protecting cherub'): how has the Christian tradition often read it?
options: Both as a satire of the excessive pride of the king of Tire and, typologically, as a figure of the fall of Satan (with Isaiah 14)
As a praise of the wealth of Tire
expert.explanation: Just like Isaiah 14 on the king of Babylon ('bright star'), Ezekiel 28 denounces the hubris of an earthly sovereign through the prism of the original fall.

expert.question: What prophecy from Genesis 9:25-27 spoken by Noah foreshadows the future spiritual role of the line of Shem?
options: 'Blessed be the LORD God of Shem' and may Japheth dwell in the tents of Shem
That Ham will dominate the whole earth
That the flood will start again
expert.explanation: The blessing of Shem foreshadows the chosen lineage (Abraham, Israel, the Messiah) in whose 'tents' the nations (Japheth) will find shelter.

expert.question: In Galatians 3:16, what grammatical detail of the promise to Abraham does Paul emphasize to apply it to Christ?
options: The singular 'to your posterity' (sperma) rather than the plural 'to your posterities', ultimately designating Christ
The use of a Greek adjective
expert.explanation: Paul shows that the promise made to the descendants of Abraham finds its decisive fulfillment in the unique person of Christ.

expert.question: Which prophet foretold that the bitter waters and the desert would blossom like the daffodil/lily upon the return of the redeemed of the Lord?
expert.explanation: Isaiah 35 celebrates the transformation of the barren desert and the 'holy way' opened to the Lord's redeemed.

expert.question: In Acts 3:21, Peter speaks of the 'times of restoration of all things' (apokatastasis): on what basis does he base this expectation?
options: On the prophets of the Old Testament ('of whom God spoke anciently by the mouth of his holy prophets')
By a decree of the Roman Senate
expert.explanation: Peter affirms that heaven must receive Jesus until the cosmic restoration promised by all the prophets from the beginning.

expert.question: Which prophet announced the fall of Babylon in a famous oracle comparing its past glory to an uninhabited desert populated by wild beasts?
expert.explanation: Isaiah 13:19-22 and Jeremiah 50-51 announce the complete and lasting collapse of the Babylonian metropolis.

expert.question: In 2 Peter 1:19-21, what image does the apostle use to describe the 'prophetic word' before Christ's return?
options: A lamp that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in our hearts
expert.explanation: Peter recalls at the same time that no prophecy of Scripture is the fruit of human interpretation or will, but carried by the Holy Spirit.

expert.question: Which prophecy in Zechariah 14:4-9 describes the Lord setting His feet on a specific mountain near Jerusalem on the final day?
options: The Mount of Olives, which will split in the middle from east to west
expert.explanation: Zechariah 14:4 announces that his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives on that day, followed by the universal reign of the Lord over all the earth.
